findings.issue: Task 9 Description (line 25) and Acceptance Criteria (line 51) both say 'All 18 unit scenarios in TelegramSenderTest are present' — but the Details audit catalog (lines 94-145) now explicitly lists 28 discrete unit @Test methods (4 happy-path + 3 five-xx + 6 four-twenty-nine + 3 terminal-4xx + 5 pre-wire-guards + 2 timeouts + 5 token-leak = 28). The headline 18 in Description and AC are not updated to reflect the expanded catalog. An executing agent reading Description/AC will believe 18 is the full target, potentially stopping short and missing the 10 additional scenarios (pre-wire guards, timeouts, per-site token-leak tests). The jq assertion at line 90 uses `length >= 28` but the comment explains it as '18 unit + 4 integration + 3 BotServiceTest + 2 BotControllerIT + 1 BotRepositoryTest = 28' — which is arithmetic for a floor of 28 total across all files, not 28 unit-only. In practice if the agent emits one entry per catalog item the threshold will be 38 (28 unit + 10 others), so the jq assertion would under-guard.
findings.fix: Update Description line 25 and AC line 51 from '18 unit scenarios' to '28 unit scenarios'. Update the jq assertion comment to reflect the real count: 28 unit + 4 integration + 3 BotServiceTest + 2 BotControllerIT + 1 BotRepositoryTest = 38, and raise the threshold to `length >= 38`.

findings.issue: Task 8 Verification Steps (line 92) still uses 'python' to validate the JSON report file: `python -c "import json; json.load(open('work/...'))"`'. On this system 'python' resolves to Anaconda Python so it works, but a CI environment or a developer without Anaconda may have only 'python3' or neither. The previous iteration flagged this as minor; it remains unfixed. Task 7 uses `jq .` which is portable and already present on this system.
